_note: How the Europe map's fields become one terrain word per hex. Each hex is measured over its own pixels: 'ground' is its share of dry land, 'lake' its share of lake; 'relief', 'woods', 'marsh', 'sand', 'grass' are averages over its dry land, on the same 0..1 scales the painter uses; 'cover' is the dominant ground cover at its centre. Classes are tried in order and the first that matches wins. Thresholds are a first reading and are meant to be tuned with integration. At 120 km a hex is larger than Malta and wider than the Bosporus. 'keep_land' names places that must be land although they fill less of their hex than the rule asks; 'waters' and 'passages' are named points used to report which seas the sea hexes join and where a strait is narrower than a hex. These three lists are proposals for integration and the Owner to prune. 'open_edges' are map edges beyond which the sea continues: water reaching them counts as one ocean.

keep_land.name: Malta
keep_land.why: Taken by Bonaparte in 1798 and by Britain in 1800; its return was the open quarrel of 1803.

keep_land.name: Corfu
keep_land.why: Key of the Ionian Islands, which changed hands four times in the period.

keep_land.name: Minorca
keep_land.why: Port Mahon, British naval base 1798-1802; stands for the Balearics.

keep_land.name: Palermo
keep_land.why: Western Sicily: seat of the Bourbon court under British protection, 1806-15.

keep_land.name: Crete
keep_land.why: Ottoman island commanding the southern Aegean.

keep_land.name: Cyprus
keep_land.why: Ottoman island off the Levant coast.

keep_land.name: Gotland
keep_land.why: Occupied by Russia in 1808; the only large island in the open Baltic.

keep_land.name: Naples
keep_land.why: A capital whose hex is mostly bay.

keep_land.name: Amsterdam
keep_land.why: Holland north of the rivers, half Zuiderzee at this scale.

keep_land.name: Cádiz
keep_land.why: Besieged 1810-12 while seat of the Cortes; the hex is mostly gulf.

keep_land.name: Acre
keep_land.why: The siege of 1799; the coastal hex is mostly sea.
